ins621.whatItIs: The sodium salt of glutamic acid, an amino acid found naturally in tomatoes, cheese, and mushrooms.
ins621.whyUsed: Added to savory foods like instant noodles, soups, and chips to enhance savory umami flavor.
ins621.concerns: Extensively evaluated by international food safety authorities and found safe for general consumption. Some individuals report temporary sensitivity symptoms such as mild headaches.
ins621.regulatoryNote: Permitted by FSSAI within specified limits for packaged savory products with mandatory label declaration.

ins627.whatItIs: A flavor-enhancing nucleotide salt produced from yeast extract or dried fish.
ins627.whyUsed: Works synergistically with MSG to create a rich, savory taste in seasonings and snacks.
ins627.concerns: Considered safe by food safety agencies. Individuals with gout or uric acid kidney stones may wish to moderate intake as purines metabolize to uric acid.
ins627.regulatoryNote: Permitted food additive under FSSAI regulations.

ins327.whatItIs: A calcium salt of lactic acid used as a food firming agent, buffering salt, and acidity regulator.
ins327.whyUsed: Fortifies foods with calcium, stabilizes food texture in baked goods, and controls acidity.
ins327.concerns: Generally Recognized As Safe (GRAS) by FSSAI and FDA. Excellent source of dietary calcium.
ins327.regulatoryNote: Permitted food additive under FSSAI and Codex Alimentarius.

ins631.whatItIs: A flavor enhancer salt naturally present in meat and fish extracts.
ins631.whyUsed: Boosts umami depth when combined with monosodium glutamate in instant noodles and savory snacks.
ins631.concerns: Recognized as safe worldwide. Metabolized into purines, so individuals watching uric acid levels should note its presence.
ins631.regulatoryNote: Approved food additive by FSSAI and EFSA.

ins211.whatItIs: A sodium salt of benzoic acid used globally to inhibit yeast, mold, and bacteria in acidic foods.
ins211.whyUsed: Extends shelf life of soft drinks, sauces, pickles, and fruit juices.
ins211.concerns: Generally recognized as safe within regulatory thresholds. When combined with ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) under heat, trace benzene can form, though levels are monitored and kept strictly low.
ins211.regulatoryNote: Permitted by FSSAI with maximum residual limit restrictions.

ins202.whatItIs: The potassium salt of sorbic acid, a compound naturally occurring in rowan berries.
ins202.whyUsed: Prevents mold and yeast growth in baked goods, cheeses, syrups, and beverages.
ins202.concerns: Well-studied additive broken down in the human body into water and carbon dioxide like natural fatty acids.
ins202.regulatoryNote: Widely permitted by FSSAI, US FDA, and EFSA.

ins223.whatItIs: An inorganic sodium compound that acts as a disinfectant, antioxidant, and preservative.
ins223.whyUsed: Prevents browning in dried fruits and preserves crispness in processed potato and biscuit products.
ins223.concerns: Releases sulfur dioxide gas which can provoke respiratory tightness or asthma attacks in sulfite-sensitive individuals.
ins223.regulatoryNote: FSSAI permitted with mandatory allergen advisory if sulfites exceed 10 ppm.

ins330.whatItIs: An organic acid found naturally in citrus fruits like lemons and limes.
ins330.whyUsed: Adds a sharp tart taste and acts as an antioxidant and pH regulator in beverages and candies.
ins330.concerns: Safe and naturally present in human metabolism. Frequent consumption of highly acidic soft drinks may contribute to tooth enamel erosion.
ins330.regulatoryNote: FSSAI approved as Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) ingredient.

ins102.whatItIs: A synthetic lemon yellow azo dye used to impart bright golden color.
ins102.whyUsed: Gives soft drinks, instant noodles, confectioneries, and snacks a bright yellow appearance.
ins102.concerns: May cause intolerance reactions (hives, nasal congestion) particularly in individuals sensitive to aspirin. European regulations require a warning regarding hyperactivity in children.
ins102.regulatoryNote: FSSAI permits synthetic colors up to 100 mg/kg in specific food categories.

ins110.whatItIs: A synthetic petroleum-derived orange-red azo dye.
ins110.whyUsed: Provides orange hues to beverages, jellies, packaged sweets, and snack foods.
ins110.concerns: Associated with mild allergic symptoms in sensitive individuals. Restricted or flagged for children's focus in EU guidelines.
ins110.regulatoryNote: Permitted under FSSAI regulations with strict concentration limits.

ins122.whatItIs: A synthetic red azo dye producing rich red to maroon tones.
ins122.whyUsed: Used in candies, ice creams, jams, and carbonated drinks for red coloring.
ins122.concerns: Subject to strict regulatory limits due to potential hypersensitivity reactions in asthmatic individuals.
ins122.regulatoryNote: Approved by FSSAI; banned in the United States by the US FDA.

ins124.whyUsed: Adds vivid red tones to packaged sweets, sauces, canned cherries, and soft drinks.
ins124.concerns: Evaluated by EFSA and assigned a low acceptable daily intake (ADI). May trigger mild allergic responses in sensitive groups.
ins124.regulatoryNote: FSSAI approved for specified food products up to prescribed limits.

ins129.whatItIs: A dark red synthetic azo dye widely used in food and cosmetics.
ins129.whyUsed: Imparts deep red coloring to snacks, gelatins, pastries, and sodas.
ins129.concerns: Generally tolerated but monitored due to potential behavioral hyperactivity links in children when combined with other food dyes.

ins133.whatItIs: A synthetic triphenylmethane dye producing a bright blue shade.
ins133.whyUsed: Used in confectionery, ice pops, blue beverages, and cake decorations.
ins133.concerns: Poorly absorbed in the gastrointestinal tract and mostly excreted unchanged. Rare skin sensitivity reported.
ins133.regulatoryNote: Permitted by FSSAI, US FDA, and EFSA within safe limits.

ins322.whatItIs: A natural fatty substance extracted primarily from soybeans, sunflower seeds, or egg yolks.
ins322.whyUsed: Keeps oil and water blended smoothly in chocolates, baked goods, and spreads.
ins322.concerns: Safe and nutritional lipid constituent. Highly refined soy lecithin contains minimal soy protein but may affect highly sensitive soy allergy sufferers.

names: mono and diglycerides of fatty acids
ins471.plainName: Mono- and Diglycerides of Fatty Acids
ins471.whatItIs: Fats derived from plant oils (such as palm oil) or animal fats that act as emulsifying agents.
ins471.whyUsed: Improves texture, extends softness in bread, and prevents oil separation in peanut butter and ice creams.
ins471.concerns: Digested by the body in the same manner as standard dietary fats. Source (plant vs animal) may be of interest for vegetarians.

ins481.whatItIs: A food-grade emulsifier synthesized from stearic acid and lactic acid.
ins481.whyUsed: Strengthens bread dough and increases loaf volume while keeping baked goods soft.
ins481.concerns: Metabolized into lactic acid and stearic acid, both natural human metabolites. High safety profile.

ins412.whatItIs: A natural soluble dietary fiber extracted from the seeds of the guar bean plant (cluster bean).
ins412.whyUsed: Thickens sauces, ice creams, and gluten-free breads to create smooth, stable texture.
ins412.concerns: Safe dietary fiber. Excessive consumption may cause mild intestinal gas or bloating in sensitive digestions.

ins415.whatItIs: A natural polysaccharide created by fermenting simple sugars with Xanthomonas campestris bacteria.
ins415.whyUsed: Provides viscosity and prevents ingredient separation in salad dressings, sauces, and gluten-free baking.
ins415.concerns: Widely tested and approved as safe. High intakes can have a mild laxative effect due to soluble fiber properties.

ins440.whatItIs: A natural structural starch found in fruit cell walls, especially apples and citrus peels.
ins440.whyUsed: Forms gel structure in jams, jellies, fruit fillings, and yogurt drinks.
ins440.concerns: Natural plant dietary fiber with proven safety and prebiotic benefits for gut microflora.

ins296.whatItIs: An organic dicarboxylic acid found naturally in green apples and grapes.
ins296.whyUsed: Imparts a sour apple flavor and enhances fruit tastes in candies, beverages, and snack coatings.
ins296.concerns: Essential intermediate in human cellular energy production (Krebs cycle). Completely safe.

ins500.whatItIs: A mineral salt composed of sodium ions and bicarbonate ions.
ins500.whyUsed: Releases carbon dioxide gas when heated or mixed with acids, making dough and batters rise.
ins500.concerns: Common household baking ingredient. Contributes to dietary sodium intake.

ins950.whatItIs: A calorie-free synthetic sweetener about 200 times sweeter than sucrose.
ins950.whyUsed: Sweetens zero-calorie sodas, protein powders, and sugar-free desserts.
ins950.concerns: Approved by US FDA, EFSA, and WHO JECFA after extensive toxicological testing. Scientists continue to study long-term microbiome impacts.
ins950.regulatoryNote: Permitted by FSSAI with mandatory sweetener warning label.

ins951.whatItIs: A low-calorie artificial dipeptide sweetener composed of aspartic acid and phenylalanine.
ins951.whyUsed: Provides intense sweetness without sugar calories in diet soft drinks and chewing gums.
ins951.concerns: Must be avoided by individuals with Phenylketonuria (PKU) because they cannot metabolize phenylalanine. WHO IARC classifies it as 'possibly carcinogenic' (Group 2B), while reaffirming safe daily intake limits.
ins951.regulatoryNote: FSSAI requires warning label: 'Contains Aspartame - Not recommended for children'.

ins955.whatItIs: A zero-calorie artificial sweetener made by selectively chlorinating sugar molecules.
ins955.whyUsed: Stable under heat, so used in low-sugar baked products, drinks, and syrups.
ins955.concerns: Passes through the human digestive system largely unabsorbed. Extensively tested and approved by major safety agencies.

ins551.whatItIs: A natural oxide of silicon found in quartz, plants, and water.
ins551.whyUsed: Prevents powders like instant coffee, spice mixes, and milk powder from clumping together.
ins551.concerns: Indigestible mineral powder that passes through the body without accumulation.

ins554.whatItIs: A synthetic aluminum salt of sodium silicate.
ins554.whyUsed: Keeps dry food powders and table salt flowing freely in humid environments.
ins554.concerns: Contains trace aluminum. Dietary exposure is monitored by EFSA to stay within tolerable weekly intake guidelines.
ins554.regulatoryNote: FSSAI limits aluminum-containing food additives strictly.

palmoil.whatItIs: An edible vegetable oil derived from the mesocarp (reddish pulp) of the fruit of oil palms.
palmoil.whyUsed: Provides high thermal stability for frying snacks and gives texture to biscuits and confectionery.
palmoil.concerns: High in saturated fatty acids (~50%), which can elevate LDL cholesterol if consumed in excess. Environmental concerns exist regarding tropical deforestation.
palmoil.regulatoryNote: Standard edible vegetable oil permitted under FSSAI.

hfcs.whatItIs: A liquid sweetener made from corn starch processed by enzymes to convert glucose into fructose.
hfcs.whyUsed: Cheaper sweetener option that enhances moistness and browning in soft drinks and baked products.
hfcs.concerns: High intake of concentrated fructose is associated with increased risks of fatty liver, obesity, and insulin resistance compared to intact whole foods.

hydrogenatedfat.whatItIs: Liquid vegetable oil converted into solid fat by chemically adding hydrogen atoms under high pressure.
hydrogenatedfat.whyUsed: Increases product shelf stability and creates crispy texture in bakery items and fried snacks.
hydrogenatedfat.concerns: Partial hydrogenation generates industrial trans-fatty acids, which strongly increase heart disease risk by increasing LDL cholesterol and lowering HDL cholesterol.
hydrogenatedfat.regulatoryNote: FSSAI mandates industrial trans-fat limit under 2% in all fats and oils.

maltodextrin.whatItIs: A easily digestible plant carbohydrate produced from enzymatic hydrolysis of corn, rice, or potato starch.
maltodextrin.whyUsed: Used as a bulking agent, carrier for flavors, and texture builder in instant soups and snack seasonings.
maltodextrin.concerns: Has a high glycemic index (GI 85-105), causing rapid blood sugar spikes similar to pure glucose. People managing diabetes should account for it.

whey.whatItIs: The liquid remaining after milk has been curdled and strained during cheese manufacturing.
whey.whyUsed: Adds protein, improves browning, and builds texture in biscuits, chocolates, and infant formulas.
whey.concerns: Contains milk proteins and lactose. Must be avoided by persons with milk protein allergies or severe lactose intolerance.
whey.regulatoryNote: Standard dairy derivative recognized by FSSAI.

casein.whatItIs: The predominant protein family found in mammalian milk (~80% of cow milk protein).
casein.whyUsed: Enhances protein content, texture, and emulsification in processed cheese, creamers, and meats.
casein.concerns: Primary allergen trigger in dairy allergies. Must be strictly avoided by milk-allergic individuals.

soylecithin.whatItIs: A phospholipid mixture isolated from soybean oil processing.
soylecithin.whyUsed: Prevents cocoa and fat separation in chocolate and improves dough handling in biscuits.
soylecithin.concerns: Contains soy derivative. Highly refined oil fraction containing negligible protein, but flagged for soy allergies.

maida.whatItIs: Finely milled wheat flour where the bran and germ have been removed during refining.
maida.whyUsed: Primary base ingredient for noodles, biscuits, breads, and Indian bakery snacks.
maida.concerns: High glycemic index carbohydrate lacking natural bran fiber. Contains gluten protein.

ins150d.whatItIs: A dark brown food color manufactured by heating carbohydrates in the presence of sulfite and ammonium compounds.
ins150d.whyUsed: Provides rich brown color to cola drinks, sauces, gravies, and baked goods.
ins150d.concerns: Manufacturing process creates trace 4-MEI (4-methylimidazole). Safety thresholds established by EFSA and FDA ensure typical consumption is safe.
ins150d.regulatoryNote: Permitted under FSSAI with maximum numerical limits.

ins300.whatItIs: A naturally occurring organic compound with antioxidant properties, identical to Vitamin C.
ins300.whyUsed: Prevents oxidation and discoloration in fruit juices and acts as a dough conditioner in flour.
ins300.concerns: Essential human nutrient. Completely safe at dietary levels.

ins319.whatItIs: A synthetic aromatic organic compound used as an antioxidant for unsaturated fats.
ins319.whyUsed: Extends oil shelf life and delays rancidity in fried noodles, chips, and crackers.
ins319.concerns: Safe within strict allowable intake levels (ADI 0.7 mg/kg). Very high experimental doses show cellular oxidative stress.
ins319.regulatoryNote: Permitted by FSSAI up to 200 mg/kg of fat content.

ins320.whatItIs: A synthetic waxy solid antioxidant consisting of a mixture of two isomeric organic compounds.
ins320.whyUsed: Prevents rancidity and odor changes in fat-containing foods like butter, cereals, and snacks.
ins320.concerns: Approved by US FDA and EFSA within strict limits. Under continuous evaluation for endocrine safety.
ins320.regulatoryNote: FSSAI limits BHA usage to specific maximum concentrations.

ins321.whatItIs: A lipophilic organic derivative of phenol useful for its antioxidant properties.
ins321.whyUsed: Preserves food fat stability, flavor, and color in vegetable oils, chewing gums, and cereals.
ins321.concerns: Tolerated well within legal limits. Consumer preference has encouraged replacement with natural tocopherols.
ins321.regulatoryNote: Permitted by FSSAI within numerical limits.

ins407.whatItIs: A family of natural linear sulfated polysaccharides extracted from edible red seaweeds.
ins407.whyUsed: Gels, thickens, and stabilizes milk proteins in chocolate milk, ice cream, and deli meats.
ins407.concerns: Food-grade carrageenan is approved globally. Degraded carrageenan (poligeenan, not used in food) causes intestinal inflammation.

ins420.whatItIs: A slow-metabolizing sugar alcohol found naturally in apples, pears, and peaches.
ins420.whyUsed: Keeps food moist and provides reduced-calorie sweetness in sugar-free confectioneries.
ins420.concerns: Excess consumption (>20g per day) can produce osmotic laxative effects and abdominal cramping.

ins422.whatItIs: A simple polyol compound, clear and odorless liquid naturally present in plant and animal lipids.
ins422.whyUsed: Retains moisture in soft-baked cookies, energy bars, and cake icings.
ins422.concerns: Non-toxic metabolite safely processed by the body.

ins450.whatItIs: A buffered inorganic phosphate salt mixture.
ins450.whyUsed: Acts as a slow-acting leavening acid in baking powders and processed meats.
ins450.concerns: Excessive overall phosphate intake in high-processed diets is evaluated for kidney and bone health.
ins450.regulatoryNote: Permitted by FSSAI within total dietary phosphate limits.

ins452.whatItIs: Inorganic polymers of phosphate ions bonded together.
ins452.whyUsed: Improves water retention in processed meats and prevents ice crystal growth in frozen foods.
ins452.concerns: Safe within established daily intake thresholds.

ins466.whatItIs: A water-soluble cellulose derivative produced from wood pulp and cotton lint.
ins466.whyUsed: Thickens ice creams, salad dressings, and bakery glazes without adding calories.
ins466.concerns: Indigestible soluble fiber that passes safely through the gut.

ins503.whatItIs: An inorganic chemical compound used traditionally in biscuit baking.
ins503.whyUsed: Provides quick gas release for extra crispiness in flat baked goods like crackers and biscuits.
ins503.concerns: Fully dissipates as ammonia and carbon dioxide gas during high-temperature baking, leaving no harmful residue.

ins508.whatItIs: A metal halide salt composed of potassium and chlorine.
ins508.whyUsed: Replaces sodium chloride (table salt) in low-sodium packaged foods and sports drinks.
ins508.concerns: Essential dietary electrolyte. Individuals with severe kidney disease or on potassium-sparing medications should monitor high intake.

ins965.whatItIs: A sugar alcohol produced by hydrogenation of maltose obtained from starch.
ins965.whyUsed: Provides 75-90% of the sweetness of sugar with fewer calories in sugar-free chocolates.
ins965.concerns: Has a moderate GI (~35). Can cause gastrointestinal discomfort or laxative effect if eaten in large amounts.

ins967.whatItIs: A naturally occurring five-carbon sugar alcohol extracted from birch bark and corn cobs.
ins967.whyUsed: Provides dental health benefits (inhibits cavity bacteria) and sweetness in sugar-free gums and mints.
ins967.concerns: Highly toxic to dogs (causes rapid insulin surge); completely safe for humans, though large amounts cause bloating.

ins1100.whatItIs: A natural enzyme protein that breaks down complex starch molecules into simple sugars.
ins1100.whyUsed: Accelerates yeast fermentation and improves dough rise in commercial bread baking.
ins1100.concerns: Inactivated completely by oven heat during baking. Safe enzyme additive.

ins1422.whatItIs: Food starch chemically treated with acetic anhydride and adipic acid.
ins1422.whyUsed: Provides heat, freeze, and acid stability in sauces, soups, and ready-to-eat meals.
ins1422.concerns: Digested in the same manner as natural starches. Recognized safe by EFSA and JECFA.

ins903.whatItIs: A natural plant wax obtained from the leaves of the Copernicia prunifera palm tree.
ins903.whyUsed: Gives a shiny protective coating to candies, coated chocolates, and pills.
ins903.concerns: Indigestible plant wax excreted naturally. Non-toxic.

ins331.whatItIs: The sodium salt of citric acid.
ins331.whyUsed: Regulates acidity in sodas and acts as an emulsifying salt in melted cheese spreads.
ins331.concerns: Naturally metabolized salt with high safety margin.

ins338.whatItIs: A mineral inorganic acid used widely in dark cola drinks.
ins338.whyUsed: Imparts a sharp, tangy flavor bite and acts as a preservative in cola beverages.
ins338.concerns: High consumption of dark sodas containing phosphoric acid is linked with lower bone mineral density and tooth decay.
ins338.regulatoryNote: Permitted by FSSAI in carbonated beverages up to prescribed limits.

ins339.whatItIs: Inorganic salt of sodium and phosphate.
ins339.whyUsed: Prevents coagulation in condensed milk and acts as a buffer in pudding mixes.
ins339.concerns: Safe within daily mineral intake guidelines.

ins341.whatItIs: Calcium salts of phosphoric acid naturally present in bones and milk.
ins341.whyUsed: Conditioner in bread flour and calcium fortifier in fruit drinks.

ins282.whatItIs: The calcium salt of propionic acid.
ins282.whyUsed: Inhibits mold and rope bacteria in commercial bread and bakery products.
ins282.concerns: Metabolized naturally like short-chain fatty acids. Rare anecdotal irritability reported in sensitive children.

ins200.whatItIs: A natural organic compound first isolated from unripe rowanberries.
ins200.whyUsed: Prevents mold and yeast development in cheese, wine, and baked goods.
ins200.concerns: Extremely low toxicity; broken down into carbon dioxide and water.

ins160a.whatItIs: A strongly colored red-orange pigment abundant in carrots and plants.
ins160a.whyUsed: Provides natural yellow to orange hues and Provitamin A fortification in butter, margarine, and drinks.

ins160c.whatItIs: An oil-soluble extract from the fruits of Capsicum annuum (red peppers).
ins160c.whyUsed: Imparts warm red-orange coloring to seasonings, snacks, and processed meats.
ins160c.concerns: Natural spice extract with high safety record.

ins100.whatItIs: The principal curcuminoid of the popular Indian spice turmeric (Curcuma longa).
ins100.whyUsed: Adds bright yellow coloring and mild herbal flavor to soups, mustards, and snacks.
ins100.concerns: Natural phytochemical widely consumed in traditional cooking.

cocoasolids.whatItIs: The non-fat component of cocoa beans after pressing out cocoa butter.
cocoasolids.whyUsed: Gives chocolate flavor and dark color to confectionery, biscuits, and milk drinks.
cocoasolids.concerns: Contains small amounts of natural caffeine and theobromine stimulant compounds.
cocoasolids.regulatoryNote: Standard agricultural food ingredient under FSSAI.

milksolids.whatItIs: The dried mineral, protein, and carbohydrate solids of cow or buffalo milk.
milksolids.whyUsed: Builds creaminess and flavor richness in chocolates, ice creams, and baked products.
milksolids.concerns: Must be avoided by people with milk protein allergies or lactose intolerance.
milksolids.regulatoryNote: Standard dairy ingredient regulated by FSSAI.

invertsugar.whatItIs: A mixture of glucose and fructose produced by splitting sucrose with heat or acids.
invertsugar.whyUsed: Prevents sugar crystallization and retains moisture in soft cookies and sweets.
invertsugar.concerns: Concentrated simple sugar; contributes to daily caloric sugar limit.

iodizedsalt.whatItIs: Sodium chloride fortified with potassium iodate to prevent iodine deficiency.
iodizedsalt.whyUsed: Essential flavor enhancer and natural food preservative.
iodizedsalt.concerns: High dietary sodium intake is associated with elevated blood pressure. Excessive intake should be avoided.
iodizedsalt.regulatoryNote: Mandated by FSSAI for direct human consumption to combat goiter.

names: diacetyl tartaric acid esters of mono and diglycerides
ins472e.whatItIs: An emulsifier derived from tartaric acid and mono- and diglycerides.
ins472e.whyUsed: Strengthens bread gluten network for improved dough elasticity and oven spring.
ins472e.concerns: Fully metabolized into standard dietary organic acids and fats.

ins476.whatItIs: An emulsifier made from glycerol and castor bean fatty acids.
ins476.whyUsed: Reduces viscosity in liquid chocolate, allowing smoother flow during manufacturing.
ins476.concerns: Safe within established numerical daily intake limits.

ins516.whatItIs: A naturally occurring inorganic calcium mineral salt.
ins516.whyUsed: Coagulant in tofu production and dough conditioner in yeast breads.

ins470i.whatItIs: Salts formed from stearic acid and minerals like magnesium or calcium.
ins470i.whyUsed: Prevents ingredients from sticking to machinery during tablet candy compression.
ins470i.concerns: Commonly used in mints and pharmaceuticals; digested like fatty acids.

ins444.whatItIs: A synthetic emulsifier produced by esterification of sucrose.
ins444.whyUsed: Keeps flavor oils suspended evenly in citrus-flavored soft drinks.
ins444.concerns: Evaluated safe by WHO JECFA and EFSA.

ins1442.whatItIs: A modified food starch cross-linked to resist high processing temperatures.
ins1442.whyUsed: Thickens canned soups, fruit pies, and frozen yogurts.

shortening.whatItIs: Fat blend formulated for baking to produce flaky pastry layers.
shortening.whyUsed: Creates tender texture in biscuits, puff pastries, and cakes.
shortening.concerns: High saturated fat content. Modern interesterified fats replace trans fats.
shortening.regulatoryNote: FSSAI compliant edible vegetable fat product.

cornstarch.whatItIs: Pure carbohydrate starch extracted from the endosperm of corn kernels.
cornstarch.whyUsed: Thickener in custards, gravies, and coating batter for crispy fried items.
cornstarch.concerns: Gluten-free starch; high glycemic index carbohydrate.

ins501.whatItIs: An inorganic salt compound used in cocoa processing (dutching).
ins501.whyUsed: Reduces cocoa acidity and darkens chocolate color.

ins509.whatItIs: An inorganic compound salt of calcium and chlorine.
ins509.whyUsed: Helps canned vegetables maintain crispness and aids cheese curdling.

ins511.whatItIs: A natural mineral salt extracted from sea water.
ins511.whyUsed: Primary coagulant for solidifying soy milk into tofu.

ins901.whatItIs: A natural wax produced by honey bees.
ins901.whyUsed: Provides protective shine on gummy candies and jelly beans.

ins960.whatItIs: Natural intense sweetener extracted from the leaves of the Stevia rebaudiana plant.
ins960.whyUsed: Provides zero-calorie plant sweetness in soft drinks and tea concentrates.
ins960.concerns: Approved by WHO JECFA, US FDA, and EFSA as safe.

ins968.whatItIs: A four-carbon sugar alcohol produced naturally by yeast fermentation of glucose.
ins968.whyUsed: Zero-calorie sugar substitute with zero glycemic impact used in keto and low-sugar foods.
ins968.concerns: Extremely high digestive tolerance compared to other polyols because ~90% is absorbed in the small intestine and excreted intact in urine.

ins170.whatItIs: A natural inorganic calcium salt used as an acidity regulator and dietary calcium supplement.
ins170.whyUsed: Provides bioavailable calcium fortification and stabilizes food texture in baked goods and dairy alternatives.

cheese.whatItIs: A dairy product produced from curdled milk proteins (casein) and milk fat.
cheese.whyUsed: Imparts rich savory cheese flavor and texture to seasonings, biscuits, and snacks.
cheese.concerns: Contains milk proteins and lactose. Must be avoided by individuals with dairy allergies.
cheese.regulatoryNote: Standard dairy ingredient regulated by FSSAI.

soy.whatItIs: Plant protein and solids derived from soybeans.
soy.whyUsed: Source of plant protein and emulsifying solids in seasonings and baked goods.
soy.concerns: Known major food allergen. Must be strictly declared on package labels.

wheat.whatItIs: Cereal grain product containing natural gluten protein.
wheat.whyUsed: Base structural ingredient for baked goods, noodles, and crackers.
wheat.concerns: Contains gluten. Must be avoided by individuals with celiac disease or wheat allergies.

niacin.whatItIs: An essential B-complex vitamin required for cellular energy metabolism and nerve health.
niacin.whyUsed: Fortifies processed grains and flours to replenish micronutrients lost during milling.
niacin.concerns: Essential daily nutrient. Completely safe at standard food fortification levels.
niacin.regulatoryNote: Standard food fortificant approved by FSSAI and FDA.

reduced_iron.whatItIs: A bioavailable mineral powder used to enrich wheat flour and cereal grain foods.
reduced_iron.whyUsed: Helps prevent dietary iron deficiency and anemia in grain-based diets.
reduced_iron.concerns: Essential mineral necessary for red blood cell hemoglobin transport.
reduced_iron.regulatoryNote: Recommended grain fortificant under FSSAI nutrition standards.

folic_acid.whatItIs: A water-soluble B vitamin vital for cell division, red blood cell formation, and DNA synthesis.
folic_acid.whyUsed: Added to enriched flours, rice, and breakfast cereals for public health fortification.
folic_acid.concerns: Essential dietary micronutrient especially critical for prenatal health.
folic_acid.regulatoryNote: Mandated or recommended fortificant under global food standards.

thiamine.whatItIs: An essential water-soluble B vitamin involved in carbohydrate energy production and neural signaling.
thiamine.whyUsed: Restores natural grain vitamin levels lost during cereal processing.
thiamine.concerns: Essential nutrient with zero toxicity at standard dietary intake levels.
thiamine.regulatoryNote: Approved nutrient fortificant under FSSAI and Codex guidelines.

riboflavin.whatItIs: A naturally occurring orange-yellow B vitamin essential for metabolic cellular growth and energy conversion.
riboflavin.whyUsed: Used for food micronutrient enrichment and as a natural yellow food colorant.
riboflavin.concerns: Safe essential micronutrient excreted naturally when consumed in excess.
riboflavin.regulatoryNote: Permitted food fortificant and natural colorant under FSSAI regulations.
